points: **Nerve damage:** bacilli invade **Schwann cells**. This leads to sensory loss (temperature first, then light touch, pain, pressure), then autonomic loss (dry skin, anhidrosis), then motor loss (claw hand, foot drop, lagophthalmos).
**Definite loss of sensation in a pale (hypopigmented) or reddish skin patch**
**Thickened/enlarged peripheral nerve** with sensory loss and/or weakness of the muscles it supplies
**Infiltrated facial lesions** for 2 years (LL infiltration, early leonine facies)
**Glove-and-stocking loss of temperature and touch** (temperature lost first)
**Thickened, tender ulnar and lateral popliteal nerves**

items.name: Indeterminate
items.t: 1 or a few faint hypopigmented macules, ill-defined

items.name: TT (tuberculoid)
items.t: 1–3 **sharply defined** hypopigmented or red plaques with raised edge; **dry, hairless, anaesthetic, anhidrotic**
items.where: Thickened nerve near lesion, early damage

items.name: BT
items.t: More (5–20), larger, asymmetrical lesions; satellite lesions

items.name: BL
items.t: Many, fairly symmetrical macules/papules/plaques/nodules; sensation partly preserved

items.name: LL (lepromatous)
items.t: Widespread, ill-defined, shiny symmetrical macules → **diffuse infiltration, nodules (lepromas)**; **leonine facies**, **madarosis** (loss of lateral eyebrows/lashes), **thickened earlobes**, nasal stuffiness/epistaxis/collapse, oedematous legs, ichthyotic skin
items.where: Symmetrical glove-and-stocking sensory loss; nerves thickened

items.name: Histoid (LL variant)
items.t: Shiny dome-shaped skin-coloured to coppery papules/nodules

items.name: Pure neural
items.t: No skin lesions; nerve thickening/tenderness, sensory loss, trophic ulcers

points: sensory testing of lesions (cotton wool for touch, warm/cold tubes for temperature, monofilaments), nerve palpation, and a voluntary muscle test.

items.t: New **nerve pain, numbness or weakness**, or painful nodules with fever on treatment: lepra reaction, **urgent** specialist contact.
Eye pain or redness: same-day ophthalmology.
Thalidomide for ENL is specialist-only with a strict pregnancy prevention programme.

pearls.t: **Steroid courses** for reactions are often long. Give bone protection, GI protection where indicated, glucose and BP checks, steroid card and sick-day rules. Screen for and treat *Strongyloides* and latent TB first.

**Adherence:** the course is long (6–12 months) and skin lesions fade slowly. Explain that **reactions are not treatment failure**, and that **numbness may not recover** even when the infection is cured.
